title: Fetch API with Try/Catch in React
description: Learn how to properly handle asynchronous data fetching with error handling in React using fetch, async/await, and try/catch blocks.
learningObjectives: Implement proper error handling with try/catch
Manage loading and error states in React
Handle HTTP errors and network failures

steps.title: Set Up State for Data, Loading, and Errors
steps.explanation: When fetching data in React, you need to track three pieces of state: the data itself, whether a request is in progress (loading), and any errors that occur. This gives users feedback about what's happening and handles failures gracefully.
steps.task: Create three state variables in your component: `user` (initialized to `null`), `loading` (initialized to `false`), and `error` (initialized to `null`).
hints: You'll need three separate useState hooks
Think about what the initial value should be for each state - what should they be before any fetch happens?
The user data starts as null because we don't have it yet, loading starts false because we're not fetching yet, and error starts null because there's no error yet

steps.title: Create an Async Function with Try/Catch
steps.explanation: Fetch operations are asynchronous and can fail. We use async/await syntax to make asynchronous code look synchronous, and wrap it in try/catch to handle errors. The try block contains the happy path, while the catch block handles failures.
steps.task: Create an async function called `fetchUser` that has a try/catch block. Don't implement the logic yet, just create the function structure.
hints: Use the async keyword before the function definition
The catch block should accept an error parameter (commonly named 'err' or 'error')
You can define this function inside your component

steps.title: Implement the Fetch Logic in the Try Block
steps.explanation: Inside the try block, we set loading to true, fetch the data, parse the JSON response, update our state with the data, and then set loading back to false. We also clear any previous errors. The fetch API returns a Promise that resolves to a Response object, which we then parse as JSON.
steps.task: In the try block of your `fetchUser` function, fetch data from `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1`, parse it as JSON, and update the state. Set loading to `true` at the start and `false` at the end, and clear any previous error.
hints: Use await with fetch() to wait for the response
Use await again with response.json() to parse the JSON
Remember to set loading to true before fetching and false after
Set error to null at the beginning to clear any previous errors

steps.title: Handle Errors in the Catch Block
steps.explanation: When a fetch fails (network error, invalid URL, JSON parsing error, etc.), the catch block executes. Here we capture the error, store it in state so we can display it to the user, and ensure loading is set to false so the UI doesn't stay in a loading state indefinitely.
steps.task: In the catch block, save the error message to the error state and set loading to false. Use `err.message` for the error message, with a fallback to 'Failed to fetch user'.
hints: The catch parameter (err) is the error object
Error objects have a .message property with the error description
You can use the OR operator (||) to provide a fallback message
Don't forget to set loading to false so the loading indicator stops

steps.title: Display Loading, Error, and Data States
steps.explanation: Good UX requires showing different UI based on the current state. If loading, show a loading message. If there's an error, display it. Otherwise, show the data. This pattern of conditional rendering is fundamental in React applications.
steps.task: Add conditional rendering to your component's return statement. Show 'Loading...' when loading is true, show the error message when there's an error, show 'No user loaded' when there's no user data, and display the user's name when data is available. Also include a button with text 'Fetch User' that calls the fetchUser function.
hints: Use if statements or conditional (ternary) operators
Check loading first, then error, then whether data exists
The user object from the API has a 'name' property
The button should have an onClick handler that calls fetchUser

browserTests.name: Initial state shows no user loaded
Clicking button fetches and displays user
User name is displayed after fetch
